messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for service=canary-inference model=redwood/v13:canary region=us-west-2. p99=3200ms (SLO 1000ms), p95=600ms (baseline ~120ms). Streaming stalls increased x5. Trigger=latency-slo-breach. Pager -> devon_oncall.

devon_oncall: ack paging. I'm on it, checking dashboards now. @ben_runtime can you pull the canary routing/traffic split?

ben_runtime: looking. Current split: v13:canary=12%, v12:stable=88%. CPU on canary nodes trending 70%, GPU util ~90% on a subset of pods. I see tail lat spikes correlated with KV cache evictions. Logs: `kv_cache_evict: model=redwood/v13 shard=3 reason=memory_pressure` repeated.

alice_sre: also seeing streaming stall traces: backend stream ack delays at the inference proxy layer, TL;DR: p99 stall ~1.8s added per stream chunk. Not global 100% but high enough to push p99.

devon_oncall: ok probabilistic rollback option and rapid traffic containment. Fast question: any customer-facing errors? @leo_support?

leo_support: support dashboards show a spike in streaming timeouts for customers using long-lived streams (chat sessions > 2k tokens). Error rate jump ~0.4% for API overall, but for streaming endpoints with v13 proxied it's ~3%. Several priority customers surfaced. I'm prepping an outbound note if we need a rollback.

ben_runtime: quick mitigation options: 1) shift traffic away from v13 to v12 (recommended), 2) bump canary replica count to reduce queuing, 3) apply temporary kv cache limits to reduce evictions, 4) fall back to reduced batch sizes to lower tail latency. Rolling traffic to stable is fastest.

devon_oncall: I'm going to shift canary -> 0% for now and monitor. Command: `rwctl traffic shift --service canary-inference --from redwood/v13:canary --to redwood/v12:stable --percent 12 --mode immediate`

ben_runtime: running that now...

incidents-bot: ACTION: traffic-shift job started by devon_oncall at 3789001252. Job id=ts-20260315-01.

ben_runtime: traffic shift completed at 3789001265. Verification: v13 traffic=0%, v12=100% for this canary route. Instrumentation: p95 fell to ~140ms within one minute, p99 trending down to ~900ms. Streaming stalls rate halved.

alice_sre: nice. We're seeing improved latency, still watching tail anomalies that linger for previous in-flight streams. Those drain over ~2–3 minutes. No new evictions after the shift.

devon_oncall: good containment. Next: decide whether to roll back v13 entirely or stage a rollback plus postmortem. @carmen_prod can you assess customer impact and comms?

carmen_prod: short answer: a handful of customers had degraded streaming experience. No data loss. Recommend: 1) proactive note to affected customers explaining we detected a canary-induced latency regression and rolled traffic back, 2) offer follow-up once root cause is confirmed. I'll draft a short message for legal/comms to review.

leo_support: I'll prepare an initial support broadcast and tag affected accounts. Need a sentence confirming no API key rotations or contract changes.

ben_runtime: for root cause triage: v13 introduced a KV cache size change and a micro-optimization to attention kernel that increases memory churn under certain seq-len distributions. On some shards cache eviction + re-warm was adding 200–800ms per request at tail. Suggest reproducing with long sequences + multiplexed traffic. I captured a repro script and sample load: `scripts/repro/v13_kv_eviction.sh` (ran against a canary cluster) — logs attached in ops console.

alice_sre: also capturing kernel telemetry (L2 mem, context-switches). If the repro holds we can make two fixes: revert kv-size change or add smarter eviction + async warm-up. Immediate fix for safety is rollback v13 until we harden.

devon_oncall: agree. I'll file a rollback ticket and schedule a controlled revert to v12 in the canary pipeline. Command to rollback: `deploy rollback --service canary-inference --target-tag redwood/v12:stable --reason "latency regression v13"`

incidents-bot: TASK: rollback job queued by devon_oncall at 3789001320. Job id=rb-20260315-01.

ben_runtime: rollback executed at 3789001345. Canary now running v12 stable. Post-rollback verification: p95=130ms, p99=850ms, streaming stalls at baseline. No new customer errors reported after 3789001360.

devon_oncall: documenting timeline and impact. Summary so far: root cause suspected kv cache and attention-kernel memory churn in v13 under long-seq multiplexed workloads. Customer impact: transient streaming timeouts for long sessions (~3% of streams hitting canary) and overall API error bump ~0.4% for ~8 minutes.

carmen_prod: posting comms draft to #product-updates, sharing with support and legal. Proposed: "We detected a latency regression in a canary model rollout and reverted the canary; most customers were unaffected but some long-stream sessions experienced delays. We're investigating and will follow up."

leo_support: sent initial alerts to impacted customers with the proposed language. No escalations yet.

maria_devex: quick note for postmortem: capture the canary traffic mix, seq-length distribution, and the exact config change in v13 (kv_size=1.5x, attention-kernel=optA). I'll add an eval run to stress long-stream scenarios in CI.

devon_oncall: handing off to night oncall. Handoff summary: containment done (traffic shifted -> rollback), p99 back under SLO, customer impacts noted and contacted, root cause suspected (kv_cache eviction + kernel mem churn), rollback ticket rb-20260315-01 created, follow-ups: repro, kernel telemetry, and postmortem owner = ben_runtime. Next oncall: @alice_sre please take over at 3789001600 for final validation and postmortem kick.

alice_sre: taking the handoff. I'll monitor for 30m and start postmortem doc. Leaving this thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
